html:
Michael VIII Palaiologos was Byzantine emperor from 1259 to 1282 and the founder of the Palaiologos dynasty, the last to rule the empire. He took Constantinople back from the Latin Empire in 1261.

A noble general of the Empire of Nicaea, he became regent for the child emperor John IV Laskaris in 1258 and co-emperor the next year. In 1259 he beat a Latin coalition at Pelagonia. In July 1261 a small force under his general Alexios Strategopoulos found Constantinople almost unguarded and took it, and Michael entered in triumph. On Christmas Day 1261 he had the boy John IV blinded, for which the patriarch excommunicated him.

To fend off Charles of Anjou, who planned a new crusade to restore Latin rule, he agreed to union with Rome at Lyon in 1274, which angered most of his clergy and people. His agents helped stir up the Sicilian Vespers of 1282, the revolt that wrecked Charles's plans. He gave Genoa trade privileges and the colony at Galata. But by spending on the west he neglected the east, where the Turks soon advanced.
